name: Russia
shortSummary: Russia remains India's "Special and Privileged Strategic Partner," rooted in decades of Soviet-era defence supply, and has grown further as India became a top buyer of discounted Russian crude oil following Western sanctions after 2022.
complexity: India has maintained strategic autonomy on the Russia-Ukraine war, abstaining on most UN resolutions condemning Russia while sharply increasing discounted Russian oil imports — a stance that has drawn criticism from Western partners, including tariff pressure from the US in 2025.

majorAreasOfCooperation.description: Russia remains the single largest source of India's legacy and current military hardware.
Russia became India's top crude oil supplier by volume after 2022.
Russian-built reactors at Kudankulam form a major part of India's nuclear generation capacity.

majorChallenges.title: Western sanctions exposure
majorChallenges.description: India's continued Russian oil and defence purchases have drawn secondary-sanctions risk and, in 2025, US tariff pressure.

majorChallenges.title: Legacy defence dependency
majorChallenges.description: Russia's ability to reliably deliver spares and new platforms has been strained by its own wartime production demands.

recentDevelopments.title: PM Modi visits Moscow and Kyiv in the same year
recentDevelopments.description: PM Modi visited both Moscow and Kyiv in 2024, the Kyiv visit being the first by an Indian prime minister since Ukrainian independence, underscoring India's balancing approach to the Russia-Ukraine war.
recentDevelopments.whyItMatters: Signals India is actively managing, not ignoring, the diplomatic complexity of sustaining ties with Russia while re-engaging Ukraine.

recentDevelopments.title: Russian crude imports remain elevated despite Western pressure
recentDevelopments.description: India continued importing large volumes of discounted Russian crude oil, a practice that became a specific point of friction with the United States during 2025.
recentDevelopments.whyItMatters: The energy relationship with Russia has become entangled with India's ties to Washington, illustrating the strategic trade-offs of India's multi-alignment approach.

historicalEvents.title: Indo-Soviet Treaty of Peace, Friendship and Cooperation
historicalEvents.description: India and the Soviet Union sign a treaty of friendship shortly before the Bangladesh Liberation War, cementing Cold War-era strategic alignment.

historicalEvents.title: "Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership" Declared
historicalEvents.description: India and Russia formalise a Strategic Partnership during President Putin's visit, later elevated to "special and privileged" status in 2010.

historicalEvents.title: S-400 Triumf Air Defence Deal
historicalEvents.description: India signs a $5.4 billion deal for the S-400 missile defence system despite the risk of US sanctions under CAATSA.
historicalEvents.impact: Tested India-US relations but proceeded, underscoring Indian strategic autonomy in defence procurement.

historicalEvents.title: Surge in Discounted Crude Oil Imports
historicalEvents.description: Following Western sanctions after Russia's invasion of Ukraine, India sharply increases imports of discounted Russian crude, making Russia its top oil supplier by volume.
historicalEvents.impact: Transformed bilateral trade composition and drew scrutiny, including 2025 US tariff measures targeting Indian purchases of Russian oil.

agreements.name: S-400 Triumf Air Defence System
agreements.description: Procurement of the long-range S-400 surface-to-air missile system.

agreements.name: Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant Agreements
agreements.description: Russian-assisted construction of India's largest nuclear power plant, with additional reactor units under development.

defenceCooperation.name: INDRA
defenceCooperation.description: Bilateral tri-service military exercise between India and Russia.

defenceCooperation.name: BrahMos missile
defenceCooperation.description: India-Russia jointly developed supersonic cruise missile, also exported to third countries such as the Philippines.

defenceCooperation.name: INS Vikramaditya
defenceCooperation.description: Refurbished Soviet-era aircraft carrier acquired and commissioned by the Indian Navy in 2013.

trade.majorImports: Crude petroleum, coal, fertilisers, defence equipment

multilateralRelations.detail: Joint member of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation.
